Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed the draft and proposes the following principal revisions.

First, based on Buyer’s current diligence assessment and the limited protections in the draft, Buyer is prepared to proceed at a purchase price of USD 38,000,000. Please revise Section 1 accordingly.

Second, the agreement will need customary buyer protections, including expanded and unqualified Seller representations, closing conditions and deliverables, interim operating covenants, and indemnification provisions. In particular, the financial statement representation should not be limited to Seller’s knowledge and should state that the financial statements fairly present the Company’s financial condition and results of operations in accordance with applicable accounting standards, consistently applied.

Third, Closing should occur within 45 days after signing, subject to completion of confirmatory diligence and receipt of all required third-party and regulatory consents.

We are comfortable with the confidentiality provision in concept, subject to customary exceptions for Buyer’s representatives, affiliates, financing sources, and disclosures required by law or legal process.

Please circulate a revised draft reflecting these points, and we can then turn comments promptly.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller in writing. The Purchase Price shall not be subject to any financing contingency or post-Closing adjustment except as expressly agreed in writing by the parties.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable following the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, and in any event within 45 days after signing, subject to receipt of required third-party and regulatory consents. Buyer’s confirmatory diligence shall not delay Closing except to the extent such diligence identifies a material breach of Seller’s representations and warranties under this Agreement or a failure of an express closing condition.

3. Representations. The Seller represents to Buyer that: (a) Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than transfer restrictions under applicable securities laws or this Agreement; (b) Seller has the authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of Seller; (c) the execution and performance of this Agreement by Seller will not conflict in any material respect with any material contract, organizational document, or law applicable to Seller or the Company; (d) the financial statements provided to Buyer in diligence were prepared from the books and records of the Company and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, in accordance with the accounting principles historically applied by the Company, consistently applied, subject to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of notes; (e) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (f) to Seller’s knowledge, there are no undisclosed liabilities of the Company required to be reflected in the financial statements provided to Buyer, other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance sheet date; (g) the Company has filed material tax returns required to be filed and paid material taxes shown as due, except for taxes being contested in good faith or not yet due; (h) Seller has made available to Buyer copies or summaries of the Company’s material contracts; (i) to Seller’s knowledge, there is no material litigation pending against the Company; (j) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is not in material violation of applicable employment, intellectual property, data privacy, or data security laws; and (k) since the latest balance sheet date, the Company has operated in the ordinary course in all material respects, except as disclosed to Buyer.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement, the negotiations relating hereto, and all non-public information exchanged between the parties are confidential and shall not be disclosed except: (a) as required by law, regulation, legal process, or stock exchange rule; (b) to a party’s representatives, affiliates, financing sources, and professional advisers who have a need to know such information and are informed of its confidential nature; or (c) with the prior written consent of the other party. Each party shall be responsible for any breach of this Section by its representatives, affiliates, financing sources, or advisers.

5. Closing Conditions and Deliverables. Each party’s obligation to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to: (a) the accuracy of the other party’s representations and warranties in all material respects as of signing and Closing, except for representations qualified by materiality, which shall be true and correct in all respects; (b) performance in all material respects of covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (c) receipt of required third-party and regulatory consents; and (d) absence of any law or order prohibiting Closing. At Closing, Seller shall deliver customary officer or authorized-signatory certificates, bring-down certificates, good-standing certificates to the extent applicable, resignation and release documentation for directors or officers designated by Buyer and reasonably acceptable to Seller, and evidence of required consents. Buyer shall deliver evidence of payment of the Purchase Price and customary authority certificates.

6. Interim Covenants. From signing until Closing, except as consented to by Buyer in writing, as required by law, or as expressly contemplated by this Agreement, Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and shall not cause the Company to take any material action outside the ordinary course, including material acquisitions or dispositions, incurrence of material indebtedness, issuance of equity, amendment of organizational documents, settlement of material litigation, entry into or termination of material contracts, or material changes to employee compensation or benefit arrangements, in each case other than in the ordinary course of business. Buyer’s consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

7. Indemnification. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses actually incurred by Buyer arising from: (a) breaches of Seller’s representations and warranties; (b) breaches of Seller’s covenants; and (c) pre-Closing taxes of the Company to the extent not reflected in the financial statements or otherwise taken into account in the agreed economics. Seller’s representations and warranties shall survive for 12 months after Closing, except that fundamental representations relating to title to the Shares and authority shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations. Seller’s liability for breaches of non-fundamental representations shall be subject to a customary deductible equal to 1.0% of the Purchase Price and a cap equal to 10.0% of the Purchase Price. Liability for breaches of fundamental representations, fraud, willful misconduct, and pre-Closing taxes shall not be subject to the foregoing cap, but shall not exceed the Purchase Price except in the case of fraud. Any escrow or holdback shall be subject to mutual agreement on amount, duration, release mechanics, and exclusive recourse treatment for non-fundamental representation claims.

receiver.requested_changes:
Buyer can proceed only with a revised economic and protection package. Requested changes:

1. Purchase Price: Reduce Purchase Price from USD 45,000,000 to USD 40,000,000. In the alternative, if Seller requires a headline price above USD 40,000,000, Buyer proposes USD 42,000,000 with a USD 4,500,000 indemnity escrow for 18 months and a customary net working capital/debt/cash adjustment at Closing.

2. Purchase Price Adjustment: Add a customary Closing adjustment for cash, indebtedness, transaction expenses, and normalized net working capital, with a post-Closing true-up procedure.

3. Closing: Buyer accepts the 45-day outside period in principle, but Closing should remain conditioned on completion of confirmatory diligence to Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, receipt of all material consents, no material adverse effect, and accuracy of Seller’s representations at Closing.

4. Financial Statement Representation: Remove the limitation to “accounting principles historically applied” unless those principles are specified and acceptable; representation should be to GAAP or, at minimum, consistent accounting principles fairly presenting the Company’s financial condition and results. Remove or narrow the materiality qualifier because indemnity already includes a deductible.

5. Undisclosed Liabilities: The undisclosed liabilities representation should not be knowledge-qualified and should cover liabilities not reflected, reserved against, or disclosed, other than ordinary-course liabilities incurred since the latest balance sheet date that are not material individually or in the aggregate.

6. Compliance, Litigation, IP/Data, Employment: Knowledge qualifiers should be removed for core operational reps or, at minimum, tied to a defined knowledge group after reasonable inquiry.

7. Material Contracts: Seller should represent that all material contracts have been provided, are valid and in force, and that neither the Company nor, to Seller’s knowledge, any counterparty is in material breach.

8. Interim Covenants: Add express covenants restricting dividends/distributions, new debt, extraordinary compensation, material contracts, asset sales, litigation settlements, related-party transactions, and changes to accounting/tax practices without Buyer consent.

9. Indemnification: Survival for non-fundamental reps should be 18 months, not 12. Deductible should be 0.5% of Purchase Price, not 1.0%. Cap for non-fundamental reps should be 15% of Purchase Price, not 10%. Pre-Closing taxes should be fully indemnified and not limited by the cap. Fraud, intentional misrepresentation, and willful misconduct should be uncapped.

10. Escrow: Add an escrow equal to at least 10% of Purchase Price for 18 months to secure indemnity obligations, with escrow not being the exclusive remedy for fundamental reps, fraud, willful misconduct, or pre-Closing taxes.

11. Materiality Scrape: Add customary materiality scrape for determining breach and losses for indemnification purposes, except where materiality is used to define a listed item or disclosure threshold.

12. Disclosure Schedules: Seller should provide comprehensive disclosure schedules before signing, and Buyer’s acceptance should be conditioned on review and approval of those schedules.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Seller’s movement on closing mechanics, interim covenants, confidentiality exceptions, and indemnification is appreciated. That said, the current draft still does not bridge Buyer’s concerns on valuation and post-Closing risk allocation.

Buyer cannot accept USD 45,000,000 on the current terms. Based on the limited diligence package, the continued qualifications in the representations, and the absence of a purchase price adjustment or agreed escrow, Buyer’s revised proposal is a Purchase Price of USD 40,000,000.

If Seller is not prepared to move to USD 40,000,000, Buyer would consider a compromise package of USD 42,000,000, provided the agreement includes: (i) a customary cash-free/debt-free purchase price adjustment, including transaction expenses and normalized net working capital; (ii) a 10% escrow for 18 months; (iii) 18-month survival for non-fundamental representations; (iv) a 0.5% deductible and 15% cap for non-fundamental representation claims; and (v) no cap for fraud, intentional misrepresentation, willful misconduct, fundamental representations, or pre-Closing taxes, except that fundamental representation claims may be capped at the Purchase Price.

Buyer also requires the representation package to be tightened. In particular, the financial statement representation should not be limited solely to historically applied accounting principles without further specificity, and the undisclosed liabilities, compliance, employment, IP/data, litigation, and material contracts representations should not be broadly knowledge-qualified. We can accept a defined knowledge standard for selected matters if tied to named individuals and reasonable inquiry.

On closing, Buyer can accept the 45-day outside period in principle, but Closing must remain conditioned on receipt of all material consents, no material adverse effect, accuracy of the representations at Closing, compliance with covenants, and Buyer’s satisfactory review of complete disclosure schedules.

Please let us know whether Seller is prepared to proceed on either the USD 40,000,000 price or the USD 42,000,000 protected package outlined above. If so, we can turn a revised draft promptly.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
